title: standings() never populates Record.win_rate (always 0.0)
evidence: src/lib.rs:443-454 — the map closure computes points (wins*3+draws) but never sets r.win_rate, so every standings row carries the Default 0.0; confirmed in _factual.json raw output where all 20 rows show "win_rate": 0.0 (team_record() at src/lib.rs:405 does compute it, standings does not).
suggestion: Set r.win_rate = wins*100/matches inside the standings map closure, mirroring team_record().

title: Team filters use normalized-substring containment, risking over-match
evidence: src/lib.rs:352-355 (search_matches), 378-379 (team_record), 533-536 (head_to_head) filter with normalize_team(m.home).contains(q); a short normalized query (e.g. "america") can match any club whose normalized name contains it, conflating distinct teams.
suggestion: Use equality on normalized names (==) rather than contains, or anchor the match, for team/opponent filters.

title: Factual gate scored 0.5 but standings data is actually correct
evidence: _factual.json: assertion 'Flamengo 2019 record' marked failed with 'got row figures [6, 37, 86, 4, 38, 0, 0, 28, 90]' — these are the alphabetically-ordered Record fields (draws=6, losses=4, matches=38, wins=28, pts=90), which match the expected 28W-6D-4L/90pts; the second assertion (20 of 20 clubs, 2 Atléticos) passed. The gate appears unable to parse the Record struct's field order; dedup/normalization worked (test standings_reconcile_sources_and_team_variants passes, test_coverage=1.0).
suggestion: No code change needed for correctness; the win_rate:0.0 artifact (see standings-winrate) is the only genuine defect in that output.

title: summary/index.md claims standings does not normalize team names, but it does
evidence: summary/index.md:32 says normalize_team is 'not by standings', yet src/lib.rs:430 calls normalize_team(team) when keying the standings table — this was the exact repair the run made (prior attempt split clubs across rows).
suggestion: Update the hand-written summary note; the code correctly normalizes in standings.
